metadata.title: Evaluating Measurement Invariance of TALIS 2013 Complex Scales (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2008 teacher and principal survey data from 23 countries, which are collected under a complex two-stage sampling design (schools sampled first, then teachers sampled within schools). The authors state that sampling weights were used to account for unequal selection probabilities and to obtain correct standard errors, and that when all countries are analysed simultaneously the provided weights are rescaled so each participating country contributes equally. The paper also notes that pseudo-maximum likelihood (PML) is implemented in Mplus to accommodate sampling weights in both continuous and categorical multiple-group CFA models. No replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is reported, and the analysis is not framed as a predictive ML task where weights would be omitted for algorithmic reasons.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the paper is not estimating cognitive achievement PVs; it evaluates measurement invariance of latent constructs measured by categorical questionnaire items using multiple-group CFA (continuous vs categorical approaches). Missing data handling is described as a model-based approach under a missing-at-random (MAR) assumption using MLR/WLSMV with probit-based missing-data treatment, which is not a PV-based imputation workflow. The paper does not provide a conventional multiple-imputation procedure (e.g., number of imputations), so the exact imputation mechanism is not fully specified beyond the model-based MAR treatment.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the full available TALIS 2008 dataset for the specified 23 countries (no calibration subsample), with reverse coding and collapsing of low-response categories for each scale. The authors applied category collapsing when any response category had very low rates (threshold: <1% in any country), ensuring comparable numbers of response categories across countries. Missing responses on observed variables were handled via a model-based MAR approach within the CFA/MGCFA estimation rather than listwise or pairwise deletion.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD working paper evaluates how measurement invariance of 11 TALIS 2008 complex contextual scales (10 teacher scales and 1 principal scale) is established across 23 countries when using two multiple-group CFA approaches: a continuous approach (treating ordered categorical items as continuous) and a categorical approach (WLSMV/Theta parameterisation for ordered categorical indicators). The study uses latent variable modelling to test configural, metric, and scalar invariance, with model-data fit assessed using CFI/TLI/RMSEA/SRMR (and WRMR for the categorical model) and invariance judged via changes in fit indices (e.g., |ΔCFI| and |ΔRMSEA| thresholds). Missing data on observed variables is handled model-based under MAR, and sampling weights are applied with PML in Mplus, with country weights rescaled so each country contributes equally in the multi-group analysis. Results show that all 11 scales achieve configural and metric invariance under both approaches, but scalar invariance is not achieved under the continuous approach for any scale; under the categorical approach, scalar invariance is achieved for three scales (TBTRAD, TCCOLLAB) and additionally for TSRELAT, CCLIMATE, and SELFEF (as reported in the narrative), enabling meaningful cross-country mean comparisons for those scales. The paper concludes that categorical modelling is more appropriate for inherently categorical response formats when cross-country mean comparisons are the goal.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a methodological/technical report focused on measurement invariance testing rather than predictive modelling, so there are no ML algorithms, target variables, or predictive performance metrics to extract into main_findings. The paper also does not report a single student-level analytic sample size (it reports teacher and principal counts overall), and it does not provide per-country student counts in the excerpt, so country-level n_students cannot be populated. Confounders are not extracted because the analysis is based on CFA/MGCFA constraints and fit criteria rather than regression-style predictors.
